subject.title: fix(auth): bind OAuth and sessions to immutable identity

question: Should existing email-owned GitHub sessions and durable records be intentionally invalidated on upgrade, or must the project provide an explicit administrator-supported migration/recovery path before this security hardening lands?
rationale: The branch deliberately chooses fail-closed identity replacement rather than automatic email-to-account transfer; that protects ownership integrity but can deny access to established users and records, which is a policy decision beyond mechanical review.

options.title: Require supported migration
options.body: Keep the immutable-ID boundary, but add and document a narrowly scoped administrator migration or recovery flow plus upgrade tests before merge.

options.title: Accept recreation-only transition
options.body: Approve the stated fail-closed policy and document that affected users must reauthenticate and recreate or manually migrate legacy-owned records.

options.title: Pause the identity migration
options.body: Merge only the browser OAuth binding now and defer durable-owner identity conversion until the upgrade policy is settled.

recommendation.title: Require supported migration
recommendation.body: Keep the immutable-ID boundary, but add and document a narrowly scoped administrator migration or recovery flow plus upgrade tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposed identity transition and are the only concrete routing candidate in the supplied review context.
